rules.baseline_ovr_target: 68-72, centered near 70, derived from active Madden 27 baseline dataset

offense.question: Against a defense showing two high safeties before the snap, which clue is generally most useful for distinguishing Cover 2 from Cover 4 after the play begins?
options: The quarterback's depth on his drop
Whether the cornerbacks sink into deep-quarter responsibility or squat underneath
Whether the defensive line slants left or right
Whether the middle linebacker blitzes

offense.question: An offense uses motion and a defender follows the receiver completely across the formation. What does that most strongly suggest?
options: The defense must be playing Cover 3
The defense is likely using some form of man or match responsibility
The defense is definitely blitzing
The defense is playing prevent coverage

offense.question: A quarterback sees a single-high safety with both outside cornerbacks aligned with inside leverage. Which coverage family is most likely being threatened?
options: Cover 1 or Cover 3
Cover 2 or Cover 6
Quarters only
Tampa 2 only

offense.question: Against Cover 2, why can a route attacking the deep middle be effective?
options: Both cornerbacks abandon the flats
The two deep safeties divide the field, potentially creating space between them
The middle linebacker is prohibited from dropping deep
Cover 2 always sends six rushers

offense.question: In a standard zone-read concept, the quarterback typically leaves which defender unblocked and reads his reaction?
options: Play-side defensive tackle
Backside edge defender
Middle linebacker
Boundary cornerback

offense.question: A defense crowds six defenders near the line of scrimmage, but the offense only has five linemen and a running back involved in protection. What is the quarterback primarily trying to determine before the snap?
options: Which receiver has the highest speed rating
Which potential rusher the protection cannot account for
Which defensive tackle is strongest
Whether the defense is playing inside or outside leverage

offense.question: Why is a high-low passing concept effective against zone coverage?
options: It forces a zone defender to choose between routes attacking different depths
It prevents the defense from blitzing
It automatically converts zone coverage into man coverage
It creates an extra offensive blocker

offense.question: Against Cover 3, an offense runs a vertical route from the outside receiver and an out-breaking route underneath from the slot. What is the offense primarily trying to stress?
options: The deep middle safety
The curl-flat defender
The backside defensive end
The nose tackle

offense.question: The defense shows a double-A-gap pressure look with linebackers threatening both sides of the center. Why is this especially difficult for an offense?
options: It prevents the quarterback from using play action
It can create uncertainty over the protection's declaration and which linebacker actually rushes
It forces every receiver to run a hot route
It makes outside zone impossible to run

offense.question: Against man coverage, why is a shallow crossing route often effective?
options: It forces a defensive lineman into coverage
It uses traffic and horizontal separation to make a defender chase across the field
It prevents safeties from playing deep
It automatically creates a double team

offense.question: An offense runs four verticals against Cover 3. Which route commonly creates the biggest conflict for the single-high safety?
options: The outside vertical nearest the sideline
One of the inside seam routes
The running back checkdown
A backside flat route

offense.question: Against match quarters, the offense aligns three receivers to one side. Receiver #2 releases vertically while #3 immediately crosses underneath. Why can this route distribution be difficult for the defense?
options: It can force defenders to exchange responsibilities based on post-snap route releases instead of simply guarding fixed zones
Quarters coverage prohibits defenders from following receivers vertically
The defense automatically loses one pass rusher against trips
Match quarters requires all linebackers to blitz when #3 crosses

defense.question: An offense aligns three receivers to one side and one receiver isolated on the opposite side. What is this formation commonly called?
options: Empty
Trips
Ace
Split backs

defense.question: Why is offensive motion useful to a quarterback before the snap?
options: It can reveal clues about whether defenders are playing man, zone, or match responsibilities
It prevents defensive linemen from changing gaps
It forces the defense into Cover 2
It eliminates blitzes

defense.question: What is the primary responsibility of a force or edge defender against an outside run?
options: Chase the ball carrier from behind
Prevent the runner from freely reaching the outside and force the play back toward pursuit
Cover the deepest receiver
Blitz through the opposite A-gap

defense.question: In Cover 3, how is the deep portion of the field generally divided?
options: Two deep halves
Three deep zones
Four equal deep quarters
One deep zone

defense.question: Why is play-action especially effective against linebackers?
options: It can influence defenders responsible for run fits to step toward the line before recognizing the pass
It prevents linebackers from blitzing
It makes man coverage illegal
It forces linebackers to cover offensive linemen

defense.question: A defense wants to disguise Cover 3 as Cover 2 before the snap. Which technique could help accomplish this?
options: Align two safeties high, then rotate one down after the snap
Remove both safeties from the field
Put every cornerback in press alignment
Blitz all linebackers

defense.question: In man coverage, why is inside versus outside leverage important?
options: It determines which portion of the receiver's release or route the defender is trying to take away
It determines which defensive lineman blitzes
It changes the down and distance
It controls whether the offense can use motion

defense.question: An offense repeatedly attacks a Cover 2 defense with corner routes and underneath flat routes on the same side. Which defender is being placed in conflict?
options: The deep middle safety
The cornerback responsible for the underneath flat area
The nose tackle
The backside defensive end

defense.question: Why can a robber defender be dangerous against intermediate crossing or in-breaking routes?
options: He is positioned to read the quarterback and potentially jump routes developing underneath the deep coverage
He automatically rushes untouched
He is responsible for both outside receivers deep
He prevents all quarterback scrambles

defense.question: Against a zone-read offense, the quarterback reads the backside edge defender. If that defender aggressively crashes toward the running back, what is the offense generally trying to make the quarterback do?
options: Hand the ball off
Keep the football and attack the space vacated by the edge defender
Throw the ball away
Check into a punt

defense.question: In Cover 3, the offense runs four vertical routes. Why do the seam routes create particular stress?
options: They can attack the space between the outside deep-third defenders and the middle-third safety
They force every linebacker to blitz
They eliminate the outside cornerbacks from the play
Cover 3 cannot defend routes past 10 yards

defense.question: In match quarters, what primarily determines whether a defender continues carrying a receiver like man coverage or passes him into another defender's responsibility?
options: The quarterback's cadence
The route distribution and releases of eligible receivers after the snap
The offensive line's pass set
The location of the running back before the snap
